To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the organization domain has a greater impact on network value than the technology domain; (2) the impact of technology domain on network value depends on the openness of the network; (3) the impact of the organization domain on business model viability is greater when the network is open; (4) the impact of network openness on business model viability depends on the complexity of the network; and (5) network complexity has a greater impact when the network is closed

the viability of mobile services is dependent on the ability of the organization to select appropriate partners and manage the network, the technology to ensure security, quality of services and accessibility and the ability of the network to manage service profiles and system integration.
business model viability depends on how the interdependencies between the organization domain and the technology domain are managed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how business model design issues in the technology and organization domain are interrelated and how these interdependencies influence network value and business models viability.
how the organization and technology domains of a mobile services business model can be designed to enhance the viability of the business model.
the following research question: What are the critical design issues that have an impact on the viability of business models for mobile value networks?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
business model viability is a function of the degree of network openness and complexity in the organization and technology domain respectively.
the more open and complex the network, the more critical the design issues become and the higher the expected network value.

the more open a mobile service network is to other network actors, the more complex it is to govern, the more difficult it is to integrate with other systems, the less secure and the more complex the network, the less value is created for the network actors and the less viable the business model is.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the design of a business model for mobile services requires balancing strategic interests and technological constraints.
business model viability is dependent on the extent to which critical design issues in the organization and technology domains are addressed in a balanced way.
a business model is viable when the critical design issues in the technology domain are aligned with the critical design issues of the organization domain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the interdependencies between organization and technology domain should be considered when designing business models for mobile service.
the interdependencies between the organization and technology domain are complex and require a careful balance between strategic interests and technological capabilities.
the business model viability is determined by the degree of fit between the design issues in the organization and technology domains.
